bullets.title: Jensen Calls Marvell a Trillion-Dollar Company; MRVL Surges 18–27%
bullets.body: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang declared Marvell the 'next trillion-dollar company' at Computex 2026, implying roughly 5x upside from current levels. MRVL was up 18% in morning trading and 27% intraday, with a 57% gain over two weeks. Marvell's keynote at Computex framed AI infrastructure as 'connectivity-constrained' rather than compute-constrained, with AECs now the preferred interconnect option—a potential headwind for AAOI.

bullets.title: NVDA Market Cap Exceeds $5.5T; Demand-Supply Gap Confirmed at ~10x
bullets.body: Nvidia's market cap surpassed $5.5 trillion, widening its lead over peers by over $1 trillion. A shareholder presentation confirmed a demand-supply imbalance of approximately 10x. NVIDIA and ARM also announced collaboration at Computex enabling autonomous agent operation on PCs, and NVIDIA launched AI for Media tools including a synthetic video detector with 92% accuracy.

bullets.title: Microsoft Build: Cobalt 200 Chip, Project Solara, AION Models, Windows AI API Expansion
bullets.body: Microsoft CEO Nadella unveiled Cobalt 200 (Arm-based CPU optimized for cloud), Project Solara (unified OS/platform for AI agent devices across any hardware), AION reasoning and planning models, and an expansion of Windows AI APIs to more PCs. Microsoft also launched Foundry IQ (agent-native knowledge layer integrating Work IQ, Fabric IQ, and Web IQ) and released a mini Surface dev box for ARM developers, filling a gap Qualcomm had not addressed.

bullets.title: COHR, MRVL, LITE, GLW All Hit Highs on Optical/AI Infrastructure Wave
bullets.body: COHR reached an all-time high with one analyst noting the upgraded 6-inch Sherman, TX fab is expected to drive revenue growth and margin expansion; the author holds Jan 2028 $610 calls. LITE is seen replicating its prior $3B→$75B trajectory on CPO/pluggables and coherent waves. Broader optics sector described as 'on fire' alongside MRVL and GLW as AI infrastructure plays.

bullets.title: GOOGL Mandatory Stock Sale Oversubscribed; Capital Raise Flags Capex Pivot
bullets.body: Alphabet's mandatory stock sale was reported oversubscribed. One analyst noted Google is effectively suspending $80B in buybacks to fund AI capex—the first such pivot in a decade—and characterized the market's negative reaction as a 'don't do it' signal to other hyperscalers. LITE separately cited Google's parabolic capex as a disproportionate benefit.

bullets.title: HPE Reports First Triple Play Since 2021; Stock +30%; Analyst Downgrades Noted
bullets.body: HPE reported its first beat-raise-raise (triple play) since 2021, sending the stock up 30%. One analyst called out HPE's Juniper acquisition as the strategic linchpin for an AI infrastructure and networking re-rating. Shannon Cross at Evercore was separately cited for a negative HPE call that contributed to a $10 intraday drop at some point.

bullets.title: CRDO Earnings Confirm AECs as Preferred Interconnect, Signaling Headwind for AAOI
bullets.body: Credo Technology's earnings showed active electrical cables (AECs) are now 'the preferred' option, which fintwit flagged as a 'major problem' for AAOI. CRDO extended its beat-and-raise streak, with shares up 1.4% post-earnings.

bullets.title: Anthropic-Google-Broadcom TPU Complex: A Capital-Stack Event, Not Just Cloud Procurement
bullets.body: One analyst characterized the Anthropic-Google-Broadcom TPU relationship as a balance-sheet trade rather than a cloud procurement story, viewing it as structurally positive for both GOOGL and AVGO. Custom ASIC demand broadly is validated, but the winners are connectivity IP players like MRVL and AVGO rather than generic design services firms.

bullets.title: Intel CEO at Computex: 18A Ramped to HVM, 14A on Track; AI PC Design-Win Momentum
bullets.body: Intel's 18A process has ramped to high volume on multiple products with 14A on track, per live Computex coverage. AI PC design-win scale is seen defending x86 and pressuring Qualcomm's Windows ambitions, with MSFT benefiting from the expanded ecosystem. ASUS skipping Intel's latest chips for the 2026 TUF Gaming 16 (using two-gen-old Raptor Lake-HX) was separately noted as a weak demand signal.

bullets.title: ALAB Golden Cross Forms; Prior Occurrence in July 2025 Preceded 184% Gain
bullets.body: Astera Labs formed a Golden Cross for the first time since July 2025, which was followed by a 184% share price increase when it last occurred. Noted as a technical setup to watch.

bullets.title: SPY on Track for 9th Straight Up-Day, Tying Record; S&P 500 Up 10.7% YTD
bullets.body: The S&P 500 was tracking for a 9th consecutive up-day, tying the historical record for the longest streak. Year-to-date the index is up 10.7% through May, putting it on pace for a fourth straight year of 15%+ gains—a feat last seen in the 1995-1999 bull run. SPY was pinned near the 759 level with a massive $2B net gamma call wall at 760.

bullets.title: JOLTS April Job Openings Crush Estimates at 7.618M vs. 6.866M Expected—9-Sigma Beat
bullets.body: U.S. job openings surged to 7.618M in April versus the 6.866M consensus, the highest level in nearly two years and the largest JOLTS beat (9 sigma) on record. Quits rate fell to a 6-year low at 1.9% and hires rate declined to 3.2%, creating a contradictory picture of high demand but limited worker mobility.

bullets.title: Fed's Hammack Flags Persistent Inflation Risk; Rate Hikes May Be 'Soon' Needed
bullets.body: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said monetary policy may not be tight enough to lower inflation and that rate hikes could become appropriate 'soon' if current trends persist. She warned that waiting for definitive evidence risks requiring larger, costlier adjustments later.

bullets.title: Eurozone May CPI Hits 3.2%—Highest in Nearly 3 Years; ECB Rate Hike Appears Cemented
bullets.body: Eurozone inflation rose to 3.2% in May driven by a Middle East energy shock, topping 3.0% for the first time since 2023. Services inflation jumped from 3.0% to 3.5%, and core came in at 2.5% above expectations. BOE's MPC member Greene simultaneously signaled the case for UK rate hikes is growing.

bullets.title: Gold Overtakes Treasuries as World's Top Reserve Asset at 27% of Global Reserves
bullets.body: Gold surpassed U.S. Treasuries to become the world's largest central bank reserve asset as of end-2025, holding 27% of global reserves versus 22% for Treasuries and 15% for euros per ECB data. Multiple sources highlighted this as a structural shift in global reserve preferences away from USD-denominated securities.

bullets.title: Barclays Warns AI Rally Vulnerable to Correction; Goldman Sees AI Widening Corporate Gap
bullets.body: Barclays flagged the AI-driven equity rally as vulnerable to a correction. Goldman Sachs separately warned that AI is likely to widen the competitive gap between large corporate incumbents and smaller firms. Morgan Stanley noted AI infrastructure spend is already ~10x above early cloud cycle levels with $256T of global capital available to finance the buildout.

bullets.title: NFLX on 7th Consecutive Down Day—Longest Losing Streak Since 2022
bullets.body: Netflix was tracking for its 7th straight red session, the longest losing streak since 2022. The stock has fallen 23% since mid-April and remains 37% below its all-time high from June, after having bounced 42% from February to April.

bullets.title: NBIS: $2.7M Put Bet Signals Bearish Positioning
bullets.body: A single trader added $2.7 million in NBIS puts, flagged as significant bearish positioning in the name.

bullets.title: MLCC Supply Exceptionally Tight; China Controls High-Capacitance Supply via Rare Earth Chokehold
bullets.body: A 25-year semiconductor industry veteran noted unusual market enthusiasm for MLCCs (multilayer ceramic capacitors) due to extremely tight supply—a dynamic not seen in a quarter century. Separately, China's control of dysprosium oxide (used in 0.3%-2% concentrations in Class II high-capacitance MLCCs) gives it a structural chokehold on global MLCC supply.

bullets.title: Amazon Prime Day Set for June 23–27; TSLA May China Deliveries +39% YoY
bullets.body: Amazon confirmed its next Prime Day spans four days beginning June 23rd. Tesla's May China deliveries rose 39% year-over-year, the best two-month total since Q4 2022.
